subject: multi-species model with coefficients that vary among regions and species

messages.author: 29d930b99cef48f0
messages.subject: multi-species model with coefficients that vary among regions and species
parts:
Hello fellow modellers, 
I'm hoping I can get some eyes on this model because I haven't seen it done before, and I could use some knowledgeable folks to bounce it off of. It is a multispecies density model where density coefficients vary randomly among species and subregions, and uses offsets to account for detection probability, so no replicate surveys. 

For an individual species (i), the coefficient for a specific variable (k) varies among regions (j) according to a normal distribution with: 

  beta_ijk ~ normal(mu_ik, var_ik). 

The hyperprior for the mean for variable k (mu_ik) in turn varies among species according to a normal distribution, where: 

mu_ik ~ Normal(mu_k, var_k), 

where mu_k is the mean among all species for coefficient k and var_ik are independent among regions (i.e. not drawn from a distribution). I hope that description makes sense.  

Not being a statistician, what I'm mostly concerned with is that I specified the hyper-priors correctly between the two levels (species and region), or that maybe I should be pulling from a multivariate normal. The basic model code is below to evaluate. Thanks in advance for any help I can get. 


model{
  # Hyper-hyperpriors
  # Priors on the hyperpriors for species- and region-specific coefficients
  for(k in 1:nbeta){
    mu.beta[k] ~ dnorm(0, 0.01)
    sd.beta[k] ~ dunif(0, 5)
    tau.beta[k] <- pow(sd.beta[i], -2)
  }
 
  # Hyperpriors
  # Priors on the region-specific betas for each species
  for(i in 1: nspec){
    for(k in 1:nbeta){
      mu.beta.reg[i, k] ~ dnorm(mu.beta[k], tau.beta[k])
      sd.beta.reg[i, k] ~ dunif(0, 5)
      tau.beta.reg[i, k] <- pow(sd.beta.reg[i, k], -2)
    }
  }
 
  for(i in 1:nspec){
    # Priors
    for(j in 1:nreg){
      for(k in 1:nbeta){
        beta[i, j, k] ~ dnorm(mu.beta.reg[i, k], tau.beta.reg[i, k])
      }
    }
   
    for(j in 1:nsite){
      ldens[j, i] <- inprod(beta[i, reg[j], ], x.beta[j, ])
     
      log(lambda[j, i]) <- ldens[j, i] + off[j, i]
      y[j, i] ~ dpois(lambda[j, i])
    }
  }
}
